- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# AGENTS.md — Gossamer
2	
3	## What is Gossamer?
4	
5	Gossamer is a CLI tool that tracks AI coding sessions across git repositories. It sits on top of **entireio** (`entire`), a session checkpointing tool that commits AI agent conversation logs to a dedicated git branch (`entire/checkpoints/v1`). Gossamer adds:
6	
7	- A SQLite database (`~/.gossamer/gossamer.db`) that indexes sessions and repositories
8	- An interactive TUI (terminal UI) for browsing repos and sessions
9	- Semantic search over session transcripts via **witchcraft** (a local embedding/vector-search library)
10	- Shell integration (`gr` function for `cd`-ing into a tracked repo)
11	- Claude Code hook integration (auto-ingests sessions on start/stop)
12	
13	## Repository Layout
14	
15	```
16	src/
17	  main.rs              # CLI entry point, Clap command definitions
18	  db.rs                # SQLite connection + schema migrations
19	  config.rs            # Witchcraft assets path config (~/.gossamer/warp_assets)
20	  watermark.rs         # File mtime utilities
21	  entity/
22	    repository.rs      # Repository struct
23	    session.rs         # Session struct
24	  commands/
25	    init.rs            # `gossamer init` — repo registration, hook installation
26	    status.rs          # `gossamer repo` — TUI repo browser + new session wizard
27	    sessions.rs        # `gossamer sessions` — TUI session list
28	    show.rs            # `gossamer show` — session transcript viewer
29	    search.rs          # `gossamer search` — semantic search TUI
30	    index.rs           # `gossamer index` — full re-index from checkpoint branch
31	    refresh.rs         # `gossamer refresh` — incremental index (new commits only)
32	    new_session.rs     # `gossamer new-session` — launch agent in optional worktree
33	    resume.rs          # `gossamer resume` — resume a session (worktree-aware)
34	    clean.rs           # `gossamer clean` — delete session from DB + search index
35	    attach.rs          # `gossamer attach` — attach an existing entire session
36	    session_start.rs   # `gossamer session-start` — Claude Code SessionStart hook
37	    session_stop.rs    # `gossamer session-stop` — Claude Code Stop hook
38	  ingest/
39	    mod.rs             # Search DB ingestion: sessions, repos, embed + index
40	    claude_code.rs     # Ingest Claude Code session logs from checkpoint branch
41	tests/
42	  integration_test.rs  # Integration tests (binary invocation, isolated HOME)
43	```
44	
45	## Commands
46	
47	All commands that produce output have a `--json` flag that switches from interactive TUI to machine-readable JSON on stdout.
48	
49	### `gossamer init`
50	
51	Registers the current git repository with gossamer. Steps:
52	
53	1. Reads `git remote get-url origin` for the remote URL and derives the repo name from it.
54	2. Checks for `.entire/settings.json` or the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. If neither exists, runs an interactive wizard that calls `entire configure` and `entire agent add <agent>`.
55	3. Installs a post-commit hook (`.git/hooks/post-commit`) that runs `gossamer index` after checkpoint commits.
56	4. Installs Claude Code hooks (`~/.claude/settings.json`): `SessionStart` → `gossamer session-start`, `Stop` → `gossamer session-stop`.
57	5. Installs a `gr` shell function in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bash_profile` for interactive `cd`.
58	6. Inserts the repo into the `repositories` table.
59	
60	**Requires:** a git repo with an `origin` remote. Safe to run multiple times (idempotent).
61	
62	### `gossamer repo` (default command)
63	
64	Interactive TUI listing all tracked repositories. From the repo list you can:
65	- `space` / `→` — drill into a repo's sessions and worktrees
66	- `s` — open the new-session wizard (agent picker → optional branch → name → prompt)
67	- `c` — `cd` to the repo (only when invoked via the `gr` shell wrapper)
68	- `/` — semantic search
69	
70	From the sessions sub-screen:
71	- `space` / `→` — view session transcript (`gossamer show`)
72	- `r` — resume session
73	- `n` — create a new git worktree
74	- `s` — new session wizard
75	
76	`--json` output: `{ "repos": [ { "name", "directory", "remote", "worktrees": [...], "sessions": [...] } ] }`
77	
78	### `gossamer sessions [--all]`
79	
80	Lists sessions from the past 3 days (or all with `--all`). Sources:
81	1. The `sessions` table in the gossamer DB (sessions indexed from checkpoint branch).
82	2. JSONL files in `~/.claude/projects/**/*.jsonl` (live Claude Code sessions not yet indexed).
83	
84	Sessions from the current repo are shown first, then by recency. Interactive TUI with same keybindings as above.
85	
86	`--json` output: `{ "sessions": [ { "session_id", "session_name", "cwd", "branch", "agent", "updated_at", "backed_up" } ] }`
87	
88	### `gossamer index [--json]`
89	
90	Full re-index of all tracked repos from their `entire/checkpoints/v1` branches. For each repo:
91	1. Optionally fetches the branch from a remote checkpoint URL (from `.entire/settings.json`).
92	2. Runs `git ls-tree -r --name-only entire/checkpoints/v1` to find `metadata.json` files at paths matching `<x>/<session_id>/<number>/metadata.json`.
93	3. Parses each session's metadata and JSONL transcript, upserts into the `sessions` table.
94	4. Ingests session names, repo info, and Claude Code logs into the witchcraft search DB.
95	5. Embeds and indexes if witchcraft assets are configured.
96	
97	`--json` output: `{ "sessions_indexed", "log_turns", "session_names", "repos" }`
98	
99	### `gossamer refresh [--json]`
100	
101	Like `index` but incremental — only processes commits on `entire/checkpoints/v1` since the last indexed commit (stored as `last_indexed_commit` on the repository row).
102	
103	### `gossamer show <session-id-or-path>`
104	
105	Interactive TUI for reading a session transcript. Accepts a session UUID (looked up in DB and `~/.claude/projects/`) or a direct path to a JSONL file. Renders assistant messages as Markdown via `termimad`. Arrow keys navigate turns.
106	
107	### `gossamer search <query...> [-n <top_k>]`
108	
109	Semantic search using witchcraft. Requires witchcraft assets to be configured (`gossamer config <path>` or `$WARP_ASSETS`). Returns hits grouped by session, with excerpts showing context around the matched turn.
110	
111	`--json` output: `{ "query", "results": [ { "kind", "session_id", "session_name", "dir", "agent", "hits": [...] } ] }`
112	
113	### `gossamer new-session [-a agent] [-b branch] [-n name] [prompt]`
114	
115	Launches an AI agent (default: `claude`). If `-b` is given, creates a new git worktree on that branch first. If `-n` is given, writes the name to `~/.gossamer/pending_session_name` so the `session-start` hook can pick it up. The prompt is copied to the clipboard via `pbcopy`. Uses `exec()` to replace the process with the agent.
116	
117	### `gossamer resume <session-id>`
118	
119	Resumes a session. Looks up the session's `cwd` and git branch from the DB or JSONL file, creates a worktree if needed, and launches the agent in the correct directory.
120	
121	### `gossamer clean <session-id> [--json]`
122	
123	Deletes a session:
124	1. Runs `entire clean <session-id>` (non-fatal if it fails).
125	2. Deletes from the `sessions` and `event_log` tables.
126	3. Deletes from the witchcraft search DB.
127	
128	Accepts a session UUID, a session name, or a custom title (scanned from JSONL files).
129	
130	### `gossamer attach <session-id> [-a agent] [-f]`
131	
132	Attaches an existing session to entireio via `entire attach`, then indexes it.
133	
134	### `gossamer config [<assets-path>]`
135	
136	Shows or sets the witchcraft assets directory path. Stored in `~/.gossamer/warp_assets`.
137	
138	### `gossamer session-start` (hidden)
139	
140	Called by the Claude Code `SessionStart` hook. Reads JSON from stdin: `{ "session_id": "...", "cwd": "..." }`. Inserts the session into the DB. If `~/.gossamer/pending_session_name` exists, uses it as the session name and deletes the file.
141	
142	### `gossamer session-stop` (hidden)
143	
144	Called by the Claude Code `Stop` hook. Reads JSON from stdin. Ingests the finished session into the witchcraft search DB and re-embeds if assets are configured. Non-fatal on all errors.
145	
146	## Database Schema
147	
148	Located at `~/.gossamer/gossamer.db` (SQLite).
149	
150	```sql
151	repositories (
152	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
153	    directory TEXT UNIQUE,   -- absolute path to repo root
154	    remote TEXT,             -- git remote URL
155	    name TEXT,               -- derived from remote (last path segment, no .git)
156	    last_indexed_commit TEXT, -- HEAD of entire/checkpoints/v1 at last full index
157	    last_search_commit TEXT   -- HEAD at last search DB index (used by refresh)
158	)
159	
160	sessions (
161	    session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  -- UUID from entireio / Claude Code
162	    agent_name TEXT,
163	    user TEXT,
164	    created_at TEXT,  -- RFC 3339
165	    updated_at TEXT,  -- RFC 3339
166	    cwd TEXT,         -- working directory when the session started
167	    session_name TEXT,
168	    tokens_used INTEGER DEFAULT 0
169	)
170	
171	event_log (
172	    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
173	    session_id TEXT,
174	    message_id TEXT,
175	    type TEXT,
176	    data TEXT
177	)
178	```
179	
180	## entireio Integration
181	
182	**entireio** (`entire`) is an external tool that checkpoints AI coding sessions to a git branch. Gossamer wraps it in several ways:
183	
184	| entireio command | When gossamer calls it |
185	|---|---|
186	| `entire configure [flags]` | During `gossamer init` wizard (skipped if `.entire/settings.json` exists) |
187	| `entire agent add <agent>` | During `gossamer init` wizard, for each selected agent |
188	| `entire clean <session-id>` | During `gossamer clean` (non-fatal) |
189	| `entire attach <session-id>` | During `gossamer attach` |
190	
191	The checkpoint branch `entire/checkpoints/v1` has the following tree structure:
192	
193	```
194	<prefix>/<session-uuid>/<checkpoint-number>/metadata.json
195	<prefix>/<session-uuid>/<checkpoint-number>/full.jsonl
196	```
197	
198	Where `metadata.json` contains `{ session_id, agent, created_at, summary: { intent } }` and `full.jsonl` is the full conversation transcript in Claude Code JSONL format.
199	
200	Gossamer identifies metadata files by the rule: path has exactly 3 `/` characters and the third path segment is all digits (see `is_meta_path` in `commands/index.rs`).
201	
202	## Rust Tech Stack
203	
204	| Crate | Purpose |
205	|---|---|
206	| `clap` (derive) | CLI argument parsing |
207	| `rusqlite` (bundled) | SQLite database, bundled so no system sqlite needed |
208	| `serde` + `serde_json` | JSON serialization/deserialization |
209	| `chrono` | Date/time parsing and formatting (RFC 3339) |
210	| `anyhow` | Error handling with context |
211	| `crossterm` | Cross-platform terminal control (raw mode, alternate screen, key events) |
212	| `termimad` | Markdown rendering in the terminal (used in `show`) |
213	| `dirs` | Platform-appropriate home directory resolution |
214	| `witchcraft` | Private library (git dependency): local embedding model + vector search DB |
215	| `uuid` | UUID v5 generation for stable document IDs in the search DB |
216	| `iso8601-timestamp` | Timestamp parsing for witchcraft document dates |
217	| `regex` | Text sanitization in the ingest pipeline |
218	| `comfy-table` | (imported but currently unused in active code paths) |
219	
220	**witchcraft** is a private Dropbox library loaded via SSH (`git@github.com:dropbox/witchcraft.git`). It provides:
221	- `witchcraft::DB` — a SQLite-backed vector store
222	- `witchcraft::Embedder` — loads a quantized T5 model from a local assets directory
223	- `witchcraft::embed_chunks` / `witchcraft::index_chunks` — batch embedding pipeline
224	- `witchcraft::search` — semantic similarity search
225	- `witchcraft::make_device` — selects CPU/GPU
226	
227	The witchcraft assets path (model weights, tokenizer) must be configured via `gossamer config <path>` or the `$WARP_ASSETS` environment variable. Semantic search is optional; all other commands work without it.
228	
229	## Development Workflow
230	
231	```bash
232	# Build and install after any source change
233	cargo install --path .
234	
235	# Run all integration tests (build + run, no pre-installed binary needed)
236	cargo test --test integration_test
237	
238	# Run a specific test
239	cargo test --test integration_test test_index_with_checkpoint_branch
240	```
241	
242	Integration tests in `tests/integration_test.rs` create isolated `TempDir` instances for both `HOME` and the git repo, so they never touch the real gossamer DB or Claude settings. The binary under test is located via `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_gossamer")` — Cargo builds it automatically before running tests.
243	
244	## Key Invariants
245	
246	- `gossamer init` must be run inside a git repo that has an `origin` remote configured.
247	- All TUI commands fall back to plain text or JSON output when stdout is not a terminal (`--json` flag or piped output).
248	- The `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch is never written by gossamer — it is read-only from gossamer's perspective.
249	- `session-start` and `session-stop` are designed to be called by Claude Code hooks; they swallow errors to avoid interrupting the agent workflow.
250	- The gossamer DB path and witchcraft search DB path both respect the `HOME` environment variable, making it straightforward to test in isolation.
251

| `entire configure [flags]` | During `gossamer init` wizard (skipped if `.entire/settings.json` exists) |
| `entire agent add <agent>` | During `gossamer init` wizard, for each selected agent |
| `entire clean <session-id>` | During `gossamer clean` (non-fatal) |
| `entire attach <session-id>` | During `gossamer attach` |

The checkpoint branch `entire/checkpoints/v1` has the following tree structure:

```
<prefix>/<session-uuid>/<checkpoint-number>/metadata.json
<prefix>/<session-uuid>/<checkpoint-number>/full.jsonl
```

Where `metadata.json` contains `{ session_id, agent, created_at, summary: { intent } }` and `full.jsonl` is the full conversation transcript in Claude Code JSONL format.

Gossamer identifies metadata files by the rule: path has exactly 3 `/` characters and the third path segment is all digits (see `is_meta_path` in `commands/index.rs`).

## Rust Tech Stack

| Crate | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `clap` (derive) | CLI argument parsing |
| `rusqlite` (bundled) | SQLite database, bundled so no system sqlite needed |
| `serde` + `serde_json` | JSON serialization/deserialization |
| `chrono` | Date/time parsing and formatting (RFC 3339) |
| `anyhow` | Error handling with context |
| `crossterm` | Cross-platform terminal control (raw mode, alternate screen, key events) |
| `termimad` | Markdown rendering in the terminal (used in `show`) |
| `dirs` | Platform-appropriate home directory resolution |
| `witchcraft` | Private library (git dependency): local embedding model + vector search DB |
| `uuid` | UUID v5 generation for stable document IDs in the search DB |
| `iso8601-timestamp` | Timestamp parsing for witchcraft document dates |
| `regex` | Text sanitization in the ingest pipeline |
| `comfy-table` | (imported but currently unused in active code paths) |

**witchcraft** is a private Dropbox library loaded via SSH (`git@github.com:dropbox/witchcraft.git`). It provides:
- `witchcraft::DB` — a SQLite-backed vector store
- `witchcraft::Embedder` — loads a quantized T5 model from a local assets directory
- `witchcraft::embed_chunks` / `witchcraft::index_chunks` — batch embedding pipeline
- `witchcraft::search` — semantic similarity search
- `witchcraft::make_device` — selects CPU/GPU

The witchcraft assets path (model weights, tokenizer) must be configured via `gossamer config <path>` or the `$WARP_ASSETS` environment variable. Semantic search is optional; all other commands work without it.

## Development Workflow

```bash
# Build and install after any source change
cargo install --path .

# Run all integration tests (build + run, no pre-installed binary needed)
cargo test --test integration_test

# Run a specific test
cargo test --test integration_test test_index_with_checkpoint_branch
```

Integration tests in `tests/integration_test.rs` create isolated `TempDir` instances for both `HOME` and the git repo, so they never touch the real gossamer DB or Claude settings. The binary under test is located via `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_gossamer")` — Cargo builds it automatically before running tests.

## Key Invariants

- `gossamer init` must be run inside a git repo that has an `origin` remote configured.
- All TUI commands fall back to plain text or JSON output when stdout is not a terminal (`--json` flag or piped output).
- The `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch is never written by gossamer — it is read-only from gossamer's perspective.
- `session-start` and `session-stop` are designed to be called by Claude Code hooks; they swallow errors to avoid interrupting the agent workflow.
- The gossamer DB path and witchcraft search DB path both respect the `HOME` environment variable, making it straightforward to test in isolation.

LICENSE.txt
---README first 80 lines---
# Witchcraft

(formerly known as Rust-Warp)

This is a from-scratch reimplementation of Stanford's XTR-Warp semantic search
engine ( https://github.com/jlscheerer/xtr-warp ) in safe rust, using a
single-file SQLite database as backing storage, making it suitable for
client-side deployment. It runs completely stand-alone on your device, needs no
API keys, no vector database, no chunking strategy, no fancy re-rankers, and it
is lightning fast (21ms p.95 end-to-end search latency on NFCorpus, at 33%
NDCG@10, on an Apple Macbook Pro M2 Max, more than twice as fast as the
original XTR-WARP on server-class hardware, at similar accuracy.)

![pickbrain](pickbrain.png)

# Prerequisites #

Needs uv, make, and the rust toolchain.

# Building and Running #
To run, you will need the XTR weights released by Google Deepmind, and
this repo contains python scripts for downloading them from Huggingface
and quantizing to GGUF format. We can cheat by doing everything with Make:
```
make warp-cli
```
## Creating an index: ##

For testing, we used the BEIR download script from XTR-Warp to download
nfcorpus and check that we could replicate their results.
For your convenience, nfcorpus.tsv is included here, so you can run:
```
$ ./warp-cli readcsv datasets/nfcorpus.tsv
```
With all the nfcorpus documents imported, we can now create embeddings for them, with:
```
$ ./warp-cli embed
```
Next we create the index over the embeddings, with:
```
$ ./warp-cli index
```

All state gets persisted in mydb.sqlite, and you can abort the indexer and
it will pick up where it left off. To start over, you can just delete
mydb.sqlite.

## Querying the index ##

When you have the index, you can query it with:
```
$ ./warp-cli query "does milk intake cause acne in teenagers?"
```
And hopefully get a bunch of relevant answers. You can also try other
variations of this, instead of "query" you can also use "hybrid", which
combines semantic search with the BM25 search functionality that comes
standard with sqlite.

# Pickbrain: semantic search over your AI coding sessions #

Included as an example is **pickbrain** (screenshot above), a CLI that indexes
your Claude Code and OpenAI Codex session transcripts, memory files, and
authored documents into a Witchcraft database for fast semantic search. Ever
wondered "what was that conversation where I fixed the auth middleware?" —
pickbrain finds it, and lets you resume the session directly.

```
make pickbrain
./pickbrain auth middleware fix    # search across all sessions (auto-ingests new sessions)
./pickbrain --session <UUID> auth  # search within one session
./pickbrain --dump <UUID>          # print full conversation
```

The source lives in `examples/pickbrain/` and demonstrates how to use
Witchcraft as a library: document ingestion, embedding, indexing, and hybrid
search. To install pickbrain as a skill for both Claude Code and Codex:

```
make pickbrain-install
```
---downloadweights.py first 60---

import os
import shutil

print("importing pytorch...")
import torch
print("importing huggingface modules...")

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download, snapshot_download
from safetensors.torch import save_file
from transformers import T5EncoderModel

class XTR(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()

        encoder_model = T5EncoderModel.from_pretrained(
            "google/xtr-base-en",
            use_safetensors=True,
        )
        self.encoder = encoder_model.encoder

        self.linear = torch.nn.Linear(768, 128, bias=False)
        to_dense_path = hf_hub_download(
            repo_id="google/xtr-base-en",
            filename="2_Dense/pytorch_model.bin",
        )
        state = torch.load(to_dense_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        self.linear.load_state_dict({"weight": state["linear.weight"]})

    def forward(self, input_ids):
        encoder_output = self.encoder(input_ids)
        hidden_states = encoder_output.last_hidden_state if hasattr(encoder_output, 'last_hidden_state') else encoder_output[0]
        return self.linear(hidden_states)


print("downloading pretrained XTR model...")
snapshot_download(repo_id="google/xtr-base-en", local_dir="xtr-base-en",
                  local_dir_use_symlinks=False, revision="main")

print("loading model...")
xtr = XTR()
fp16_state_dict = {k: v.half().cpu() for k, v in xtr.state_dict().items()}
print("writing as .safetensors...")
save_file(fp16_state_dict, "xtr.safetensors")
print(f"Saved xtr.safetensors with {len(fp16_state_dict)} tensors")

shutil.copy("xtr-base-en/config.json", "assets/config.json")
shutil.copy("xtr-base-en/tokenizer.json", "assets/tokenizer.json")

SHELL := /bin/bash
.DEFAULT_GOAL := build

# Auto-detect platform and architecture
UNAME_S := $(shell uname -s)
UNAME_M := $(shell uname -m)

# Determine features and flags based on platform
ifeq ($(UNAME_S),Darwin)
  ifeq ($(UNAME_M),arm64)
    # Apple Silicon: Metal GPU + Accelerate BLAS
    CLI_FEATURES := t5-quantized,metal,progress
    NAPI_FEATURES := t5-quantized,metal,napi
    RUSTFLAGS_EXTRA :=
    TARGET := aarch64-apple-darwin
  else
    # Intel Mac: CPU-only with FBGEMM + hybrid-dequant
    CLI_FEATURES := t5-quantized,fbgemm,hybrid-dequant,progress
    NAPI_FEATURES := t5-quantized,fbgemm,hybrid-dequant,napi
    RUSTFLAGS_EXTRA := -C target-feature=+avx2,+fma
    TARGET := x86_64-apple-darwin
  endif
  PICKBRAIN_FEATURES := $(CLI_FEATURES),embed-assets
else ifeq ($(UNAME_S),Linux)
  NVCC := $(or $(shell which nvcc 2>/dev/null),$(wildcard /usr/local/cuda/bin/nvcc),$(wildcard /opt/cuda/bin/nvcc))
  ifneq ($(NVCC),)
    CLI_FEATURES := t5-quantized,cuda,progress

	lipo -create target/aarch64-apple-darwin/release/libwitchcraft.dylib target/x86_64-apple-darwin/release/libwitchcraft.dylib -output target/release/warp-macos-universal.node

content.text:
Good news — the data is rich. Each checkpoint commit on `entire/checkpoints/v1` carries `author_name + email`, and `metadata.json` already tracks `turn_id` + `session_metrics.turn_count` + per-checkpoint `prompt_attributions`. cosmos-graphql alone has two distinct authors (Scott Holodak, Stephanos Tsoucas) — so per-message attribution is real, not theoretical.

Before I code, two design choices:

questions.question: What granularity of author attribution should I implement?

options.label: Per-message (Recommended)
options.description: Store (session_id, checkpoint_number, commit_author) for every checkpoint. At render time, map each turn to the checkpoint it first appeared in, then to that checkpoint's commit author. Correct for sessions resumed across machines (different authors on different user messages within one session).

options.label: Per-session
options.description: Store one author per session (the most recent / most frequent checkpoint committer). Simpler, no per-turn mapping needed, but wrong when a session is resumed on another machine.

questions.question: How should the author show up in `gossamer show`?

options.label: Email, with bold "you" for self (Recommended)
options.description: Show the author email (e.g. `scottt732@gmail.com`) next to each user/assistant message. If it matches `git config user.email`, render as bold "you" instead. Header card lists distinct authors.

options.label: Author name only
options.description: Show display name from the git commit (e.g. `Scott Holodak`) next to each user/assistant message. No special handling for self.

options.label: Header only, not per-message
options.description: Add a "contributors" line to the Header card listing distinct authors. Don't tag individual messages — keeps the per-message render unchanged.

content.text:
Done. Summary of changes:

**`src/db.rs`** — added `checkpoints (session_id, checkpoint_number, commit_sha, author_name, author_email, last_turn_ts)` table with composite PK + an index on `(session_id, last_turn_ts)`.

**`src/commands/index.rs`** — added `build_commit_authors(repo_dir)` that runs **one** `git log --diff-filter=A --name-only --format='__COMMIT__\t%H\t%an\t%ae' entire/checkpoints/v1` and builds a `HashMap<path, CommitAuthor>`. During the per-meta-path loop, we now also `upsert_checkpoint` with the checkpoint number (parsed from path), the commit author, and the latest turn timestamp.

**`src/commands/show.rs`** — `Card::UserMsg` gained an `author: Option<String>` field. `run_at` fetches checkpoint authors via `fetch_authors(session_id)` and `attribute(ts)` assigns each user card to the earliest checkpoint whose `last_turn_ts >= ts`. The render path replaces `── user` with `── <author_name>` (email fallback when name is empty, plain `user` when no checkpoint exists).

**Data populated**: 63 checkpoint rows across 54 sessions, 2 distinct authors (Scott Holodak, Stephanos Tsoucas).

content.text:
Yep — commit subject is the trust anchor. `entireio` uses `Checkpoint: <id>` for the single-session direct commits, `Update checkpoint summary for <id>` for metadata-only edits, and `Merge remote session logs` for batch imports. Only the first kind is authored by the human who actually had the conversation. I was originally hoping `--no-merges` would handle it via the commit graph, but the checkpoint remote ships imports without their parents — so locally they look parentless and `--no-merges` lets them through. The subject prefix is what survives that.

---
name: entire-checkpoint-commit-conventions
description: entireio commit subject conventions on the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch and why commit subject — not graph structure — is the right way to identify direct (single-author) checkpoints.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On `entire/checkpoints/v1`, three commit subjects appear:

- `Checkpoint: <id>` — direct single-session checkpoint produced by entireio on the local agent's machine. Author = the human who had the conversation.
- `Update checkpoint summary for <id>` — non-content metadata edit on an existing checkpoint. Filtered out automatically by `--diff-filter=A` (it modifies, doesn't add).
- `Merge remote session logs` — batch import of many other people's sessions in one commit. Author = the importer, NOT the conversation author. Often touches dozens of sessions in one commit.

**Why:** When attributing turns to humans (per-message authorship in `gossamer show`), the commit message is the trust signal. `--no-merges` does NOT reliably exclude `Merge remote session logs` commits because the checkpoint remote often ships these merges without their parents in the local clone, so git treats them as parentless roots.

**How to apply:** When walking the checkpoint branch to map paths to authors, filter with `git log --grep='^Checkpoint: ' --diff-filter=A`. Anything else (batch imports, merges) is non-authoritative; fall back to JSONL `cwd` → `os_user` and look up the os_user in a map built from the trusted commits. See `src/commands/index.rs` `build_commit_authors` and `cwd_to_os_user`.

Related: [[checkpoint-path-shape]] for the `<prefix2>/<id10>/<num>/{metadata.json,full.jsonl}` layout the index walker depends on.

- **`src/commands/refresh.rs`** — same threading.
- **`src/commands/sessions.rs`** — selects `branch` and `repo_id` from the DB; "local" sort now matches on `repo_id` (not cwd path prefix), so Scott's same-repo sessions interleave with yours by date.

content.text:
Done — both views are now fed by the same code path and produce identical data for cosmos-graphql (60 sessions, same branches, same order).

**Why they were duplicated before**: pre-existing — they grew independently. `sessions.rs` had `DisplaySession` + `scan_claude_projects`; `status.rs` had `RepoSession` + `load_sessions`. Two near-identical DB queries, two near-identical JSONL scanners, with subtle drift (different field names, different scoping rules, different fallback merge logic).

**What changed**:
- **`src/commands/session_list.rs` (new, ~165 lines)** — owns the canonical `DisplaySession` struct, a `Scope { All, Repo(&Repository) }` enum, and a `fetch(scope, include_old)` function that does the DB query + ~/.claude/projects JSONL augmentation in one place.
- **`src/commands/sessions.rs`** — dropped its local `DisplaySession` + `scan_claude_projects` + `user_text`. Now calls `session_list::fetch(Scope::All, all)` and applies the local-first sort on top.
- **`src/commands/status.rs`** — dropped `RepoSession` struct, the entire `load_sessions` function, and `user_text`. Now calls `session_list::fetch(Scope::Repo(repo), true)`. Renamed `s.agent` → `s.agent_name` at three render sites.

Net: removed ~190 lines of duplicated logic, single source of truth. Any future fix to session listing (new filter, new column, new JSONL source) lands in one place and both views pick it up automatically.

Found it. Session `bee0c590-…` on 2026-04-09:
- **FIRST** prompt: *"Can you see what work I have on dev (past 7 days) that isn't on prod yet? I've been cherry-picking…"* — the actual ask
- **LAST** prompt: *"oof sorry I ran this: ❯ git push fatal: The upstream branch…"* — debug follow-up
- **What we display**: the LAST prompt.

**The bug**: `parse_session` overwrites `last_prompt` on every user message, so the stored `session_name` ends up being whatever the user typed *last*, not what the session was *about*. Same pattern across many sessions ("sure", "yes please", "ok fine…").

**The fix**: use the first *meaningful* user prompt instead — skipping `<command-message>`, `<local-command-caveat>`, `<task-notification>` wrappers (those are slash-command artifacts, not real intent).

content.text:
Fixed. All four of Scott's 4/9 sessions now have meaningful names taken from the original ask, not the last debug follow-up:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `oof sorry I ran this: ❯ git push fatal: …` | **`Can you see what work I have on dev (past 7 days)…`** |
| `sure` | `[Image #1] can you verify that the OpenAppWorkflow is able to perform…` |
| `fuck.. can you check the logs.. skip any flaky tests…` | `what's up with this CI run? https://github.com/…/runs/2…` |
| `ok fine .. commit directly to prod branch, push…` | `https://github.com/…/pull/4498 … https://linear.app/thecosmos…` |

**The deal**: `parse_session` was using the *last* user prompt as the session name, on the theory that "the most recent thing said summarizes where the session ended up". For long sessions that's almost always a debug/follow-up like "yes please" or shell error paste. Worse, it only worked on string-shaped content; array-of-blocks content was silently dropped, so sessions whose later prompts were arrays sometimes fell back to the metadata default.

**The fix** in `parse_session` and `parse_shadow_session`:
1. Pick the **first** user prompt with content (not the last).
2. Skip wrapper-only prompts whose first line starts with `<command-message`, `<command-name`, `<local-command-caveat`, `<task-notification`, `<system-reminder`, `<bash-input`, `<bash-stdout`, `<bash-stderr` — those are Claude Code metadata, not user intent.
3. Use a shared `extract_user_text` helper that handles both string and block-array content shapes (the old code only handled string).
4. Fallback chain: `custom_title` (explicit rename) → `first_meaningful_prompt` → `first_any_prompt` → metadata summary.

Naming is now stable across re-indexes since we always look at the same first turn.

content.text:
The data WAS populated — `bee0c590` had `branch=prod`, `author=Scott Holodak`, `agent=Claude Code` in the DB all along. The columns disappeared because the stored `session_name` ("oof sorry I ran this:\n❯ git push\nfatal: …") contained **literal newlines**, and the renderer writes the name straight to the terminal in raw mode with no sanitization. When the row reached that embedded `\n`, the cursor jumped to the next line — so branch/author/agent/id/date got written into the wrong row (or got clobbered by the next session's draw).

Both `status.rs::draw_sessions` and `sessions.rs::draw` do:
```rust
let name: String = s.session_name.trim().chars().take(name_w).collect();
let name_padded = format!("{:<name_w$}", name);
```

`trim` strips outer whitespace but leaves interior `\n` intact, and `take(name_w)` counts chars without stopping at newlines. So a 22-char prefix `"oof sorry I ran this:\n"` slips a newline into the formatted output. My first-meaningful-prompt fix made the symptom go away for *this* session (the cherry-pick prompt happens to be single-line), but any session whose first meaningful prompt has a newline would hit the same bug.

Want me to fix the renderer so it replaces interior whitespace (incl. `\n`, `\r`, `\t`) with single spaces before truncation? Same one-line fix in both draws and `session_list.rs`'s `parse_jsonl`. Belt-and-suspenders with the indexer side (which also benefits search and `--json` consumers).

content.text:
On it. Quick answer first, then code:

**Branch merges** — yes, we always point to the original branch. The branch comes from two sources, both captured at session/commit time:
1. `metadata.json::branch` — set by entire when the checkpoint was made.
2. JSONL's `gitBranch` field — captured per-turn by Claude Code as the session ran.

Neither updates when the branch is later merged or deleted. The recorded value is just a string label, so even deleting the original branch doesn't break gossamer. That's intentional: the branch tells you *what work the session was on*, not *where the commits currently live*. If you wanted "is this session's work now on main?" that'd be a reachability query (e.g. `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), separate from what we store.

Now the rendering fix — sanitize interior whitespace at the data layer so all consumers (TUI, JSON, search) see clean one-line names.

content.text:
Fix in, three layers deep:

| Layer | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Write** | `parse_session` / `parse_shadow_session` in `index.rs` | DB stores clean session_name going forward |
| **Read** | `session_list::query_db` + `parse_jsonl` | Sanitizes whatever the DB or live JSONLs hand us |
| **Render** | `sessions.rs::draw` + `status.rs::draw_sessions` | Last-resort safety so any new code path can't break the layout |

Plus a one-shot SQL `UPDATE` that cleaned the one stale row (an untracked-repo session the index pass never re-touched). 0 rows with newlines now.

**On your branch-merge question** (summary, since I led with code):
- We always show the **original branch** the session was on. Captured at commit time from `metadata.json::branch` (entire writes it) and JSONL's `gitBranch` (Claude Code writes it per-turn). Neither updates after merge or deletion — those values are just strings, not git refs.
- Rationale: the branch label answers "what was this session about?", not "where do those commits currently live?". A session about `feature/foo` is still about `feature/foo` after merge into `main`.
- If you ever want the "where does it live now?" view (e.g. "is this work shipped?"), that'd be a separate computation — `git branch --contains <commit_sha>` against the recorded `commit_sha` in the `checkpoints` table — and we have all the data to do it. Not built today; let me know if you want it.

content.text:
Found it. The branch exists on `origin` as `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1` (commit `6b720f64…`), but gossamer's auto-fetch only triggers when `.entire/settings.json` has `strategy_options.checkpoint_remote.repo` set (which would point to a *separate* checkpoint repo). cosmos-agents uses the *other* entireio deployment mode where checkpoints live on the **same origin remote** as the main repo. We never try fetching from origin, so the branch never lands locally.

cosmos-graphql and cosmos-www happen to have it locally only because someone manually fetched at some point. cosmos-agents is the first one we've seen where nobody did.

Fix: always try fetching `entire/checkpoints/v1` from `origin` too, regardless of `checkpoint_remote` config. Two cheap fetches, both no-ops when up to date.

file.content:
---
name: entire-checkpoint-commit-conventions
description: entireio commit subject conventions on the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch and why commit subject — not graph structure — is the right way to identify direct (single-author) checkpoints.
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a91b56e5-f173-4bde-b497-51eefbbc53c2
---

On `entire/checkpoints/v1`, three commit subjects appear:

- `Checkpoint: <id>` — direct single-session checkpoint produced by entireio on the local agent's machine. Author = the human who had the conversation.
- `Update checkpoint summary for <id>` — non-content metadata edit on an existing checkpoint. Filtered out automatically by `--diff-filter=A` (it modifies, doesn't add).
- `Merge remote session logs` — batch import of many other people's sessions in one commit. Author = the importer, NOT the conversation author. Often touches dozens of sessions in one commit.

**Why:** When attributing turns to humans (per-message authorship in `gossamer show`), the commit message is the trust signal. `--no-merges` does NOT reliably exclude `Merge remote session logs` commits because the checkpoint remote often ships these merges without their parents in the local clone, so git treats them as parentless roots.

**How to apply:** When walking the checkpoint branch to map paths to authors, filter with `git log --grep='^Checkpoint: ' --diff-filter=A`. Anything else (batch imports, merges) is non-authoritative; fall back to JSONL `cwd` → `os_user` and look up the os_user in a map built from the trusted commits. See `src/commands/index.rs` `build_commit_authors` and `cwd_to_os_user`.

Related: [[checkpoint-path-shape]] for the `<prefix2>/<id10>/<num>/{metadata.json,full.jsonl}` layout the index walker depends on.

---
name: entire-checkpoint-deployment-modes
description: entireio supports two deployment modes for where the entire/checkpoints/v1 branch lives — separate checkpoint repo or the main repo's origin. gossamer must fetch from both to populate sessions.
metadata:
